issues.description: Shared TritonLoraConfig.is_registered mutated from async handler without lock — race + wrong-data-structure.
issues.detail: _create_trtllm_generate_request reads and flips is_registered on a shared metadata object with no synchronization, and flips it before the backend acknowledges registration. Two concurrent first-requests double-register or one loses the race and sends a task_id with no weights. Registration state belongs in a separate registry keyed by (model, task_id), gated by a per-LoRA lock and a real backend ack.

issues.description: lora_task_id assignment is positional and collides across models / restarts.
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 and increments per entry within a single _parse_lora_configs call, with no stable mapping from LoRA identity to task_id. Across model repos or restarts the same name can get different IDs, and different LoRAs can share id 1. TRT-LLM caches by task_id, so collisions serve the wrong adapter. Derive task_id from a stable hash of (model, lora_name).

issues.description: Debug print() and traceback.format_exc() calls left in production paths.
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") fires per parse iteration, and traceback prints are sprinkled into routers and the parser's except block. These bypass the logger, spam stdout, leak internals, and cannot be filtered. Remove them or route through logger.debug/warning at the appropriate level before merge.

issues.description: Bare except Exception swallows parse errors and silently returns None.
issues.detail: A malformed multi_lora.json or unrelated bug becomes indistinguishable from 'no LoRA configured': the function prints a traceback and returns None. Operators get a silent feature regression at startup. Pick one contract: fail loud at startup, or log a structured warning with a defined error type — don't both print and swallow.

issues.description: _parse_lora_configs is a 70-line backend-branching blob; split per backend.
issues.detail: The function fuses vllm-vs-trtllm dispatch, path normalization, JSON parsing, file existence checks, and task_id assignment under one nested try/except. The data shapes per backend differ enough that two small functions (_parse_vllm_loras, _parse_trtllm_loras) over a shared repo walker would be clearer and easier to test.

issues.description: Variable shadowing and stale return type annotation in _parse_lora_configs.
issues.detail: lora_config_path is bound to multi_lora.json then rebound inside the loop to model.lora_config.npy, giving one name two meanings within 30 lines. The function is also annotated `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but actually returns List[TritonLoraConfig]. Rename one variable and fix the annotation.

synthesis.summary: The panel reaches strong consensus that the feature works on the happy path but ships two real correctness bugs and substantial debug residue. The shared-mutable is_registered flag on TritonLoraConfig is mutated from async request handlers without synchronization and without backend acknowledgment, and lora_task_id assignment is positional and non-deterministic — both will misbehave under concurrency or across restarts, with TRT-LLM potentially serving the wrong adapter. Stray print() and traceback.format_exc() calls, a swallowing except Exception, variable shadowing, and a stale return-type annotation round out the cleanup. NEEDS-WORK: separate registration state from config metadata behind a per-LoRA lock, make task_id a stable hash of (model, name), strip the debug prints, define the parse-error contract, and correct the annotation before merge.
